SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p109/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p109/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p109/r1.claim: Arabic forms can carry several functions: faʿīl may be intensive, adjectival, or passive, while a form such as مختار can also denote an action, place, time, active agent, or passive object.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p109/r1.anchor: إذن هذه الصيغة تحتمل عدة معاني. ومعروف في اللغة أن اسم المفعول من غير الثلاثي

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p109/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p109/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p109/r2.claim: In ‘to your Lord is the final settling,’ المستقر can mean the act, place, and time of settling; all are intended, with no contextual clue restricting it to one sense.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p109/r2.anchor: والمقصود من هذه الآية كل المعاني المحتملة فالإستقرار إليه ومكان وزمان الإستقرار إليه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p558/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p558/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p558/r1.claim: Arabic forms may carry several meanings: فعيل can indicate intensity, an adjective, or a passive participle; a non-triliteral passive participle such as مختار can also mean a verbal noun, place, time, or sometimes an active participle.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p558/r1.anchor: في العربية أحياناً الصيغة الواحدة يجتمع بها أكثر من معنى مثل صيغة فعيل على سبيل المثال

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p558/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p558/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p558/r2.claim: In 75:12, المستقر can mean settlement with God or by His will, the place of settlement (Paradise or Hell), and its time at the gathering; the author intends all possibilities because no contextual clue excludes them.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p558/r2.anchor: وهي كلها مرادة مطلوبة وليس هناك قرينة تصرف إلى أحد هذه المعاني

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r4.claim: Verses 7-15 answer demands to hasten Judgment: when upheaval arrives no one can flee except to God, and each must answer for every deed despite attempts to conceal it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r4.anchor: On that Day, there will be no resting place for anyone except with God.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r6.claim: The final resting place of all creation is with the Lord; Ibn Masud calls it the return and cites similar verses.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r6.anchor: {إلى ربك يومئذ المستقر} أي مستقر الخلق. وقال عبد الله بن مسعود: المصير والمرجع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r7.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r7.claim: Al-Suddi interprets المستقر as the final end, citing ‘to your Lord is the final end.’
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r7.anchor: وقال السدي: المنتهى، نظيره: "وأن إلى ربك المنتهى"

NAHHAS:v5p81/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p81/r3.speaker: قتادة
NAHHAS:v5p81/r3.claim: Qatada says al-muntahā means the endpoint.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r2.claim: The text leaves the arrival of Resurrection unstated, since the question about escape and the final return already imply that its terrors have come.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r2.anchor: وطوي التصريح بأن ذلك حلول يوم القيامة اكتفاء بذكر ما يدل عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r3.claim: The repeated ‘that day’ stresses the day they denied and states that the three cosmic signs occur together; its tanwin stands for an omitted clause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r3.anchor: فتنوين ( إذ ) تنوين عوض عن الجملة المحذوفة التي دلت عليها الجملة التي أضيف إليها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p346/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p346/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p346/r1.claim: ‘To your Lord is the final resort’ is God's address to the Prophet in worldly time, inserted to remind him of God's sovereignty over that Day.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p346/r1.anchor: فهو كلام من جانب الله تعالى خاطب به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في الدنيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p346/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p346/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p346/r2.claim: Calling God the Prophet's Lord hints that He will support him by requiting those who rejected his message.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p346/r2.anchor: إيماء إلى أنه ناصره يومئذ بالانتقام من الذين لم يقبلوا دعوته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p346/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p346/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p346/r3.claim: Al-mustaqarr is an intensified place-or-state noun derived from istaqarra, ‘to settle.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p346/r3.anchor: مصدر ميمي من استقر ، إذا قر في المكان ولم ينتقل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p346/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p346/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p346/r4.claim: Fronting ‘to your Lord’ makes the destination exclusive: no other refuge exists, as in the declaration that all return is to God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p346/r4.anchor: وتقديم المجرور لإفادة الحصر ، أي إلى ربك لا إلى ملجأ آخر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p403#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p403#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p403#2/r1.claim: The implicit meaning is that judgment or the like belongs to your Lord; المستقر is a subject whose predicate is implied by the preceding phrase, meaning the place of settlement is with Him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p403#2/r1.anchor: معناه إلى حكم ربك أو نحوه من التقدير والمستقر رفع بالابتداء وخبره في المقدر الذي يتعلق به المجرور المتقدم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p277/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p277/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p277/r4.claim: All people return to God, their final destination.

JISHUMI:v10p7180/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7180/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7180/r9.claim: Al-mustaqarr is a place of settlement, like al-maʾwā and al-mathwā, and may be temporary or everlasting.
JISHUMI:v10p7180/r9.anchor: والمستقر: موضع القرار، ونظيره: المأوى والمثوى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p661/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p661/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p661/r6.claim: The servants' fixed place may be their settlement before God, their return to His judgment alone, or their final place in Paradise or Hell, which He assigns by His will.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p661/r6.anchor: { إلى ربك } خاصة { يومئذ } مستقر العباد ، أي استقرارهم . يعني : أنهم لا يقدرون

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r13.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r13.claim: The final settlement before your Lord means the final destination.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r13.anchor: أحدهما : أن المستقر المنتهى , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r14.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r14.claim: It may mean the settling of the people of Paradise in Paradise and the people of Hell in Hell.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r14.anchor: الثاني : أنه استقرار أهل الجنة في الجنة , وأهل النار في النار , قاله ابن زيد .

QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r2.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r2.claim: Qatada explains that the final destination is to the Lord, paralleling the statement that the final end is to Him.

QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r3.claim: Ibn Masud says the destination means return and recourse to God; another view says it is the afterlife where He settles and judges people.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r3.anchor: ابن مسعود: إلى ربك المصير والمرجع

QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r4.claim: One reading makes “no refuge; to your Lord is the destination” the person’s own words after realizing there is no escape.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:12-13/r4.anchor: من قول الإنسان لنفسه إذا علم أنه ليس له مفر

TABATABAI:75:11-15/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:11-15/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:11-15/r2.claim: The final settlement is with the Lord alone: placing the phrase first conveys exclusivity, with no other refuge or barrier between people and God.
TABATABAI:75:11-15/r2.anchor: يفيد الحصر فلا مستقر إلى غيره فلا وزر ولا ملجأ يلتجأ إليه فيمنع عنه

TABATABAI:75:11-15/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:11-15/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:11-15/r3.claim: All people move toward meeting God, as other verses say they labor toward Him, return to Him, and end with Him.
TABATABAI:75:11-15/r3.anchor: وذلك أن الإنسان سائر إليه تعالى كما قال يا أيها الإنسان إنك كادح إلى ربك كدحا فملاقيه

TABATABAI:75:11-15/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:11-15/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:11-15/r4.claim: Being veiled from God in 83:14-15 means deprivation of divine honor, not lack of knowledge or physical absence.
TABATABAI:75:11-15/r4.anchor: فسياق الآيتين يعطي أن المراد به حجاب الحرمان من الكرامة لا حجاب الجهل أو الغيبة

TABATABAI:75:11-15/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:11-15/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:11-15/r5.claim: Other possible readings are that people's destination of happiness or misery depends on God's will, or that their final settlement is under God's judgment alone.
TABATABAI:75:11-15/r5.anchor: ويمكن أن يراد به أن استقرارهم يومئذ إلى حكمه تعالى فهو النافذ فيهم لا غير

TABRISI:75:12-14/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:12-14/r2.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:75:12-14/r2.claim: The final return on that day is to God's judgment and command; no one else can decide or command.
TABRISI:75:12-14/r2.anchor: أي ينتهي الخلق يومئذ إلى حكمه وأمره فلا حكم ولا أمر لأحد غيره

TABRISI:75:12-14/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:12-14/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:75:12-14/r3.claim: Alternatively, the settlement means the place in which believers and unbelievers reside, and that destination belongs to God rather than worshippers.
TABRISI:75:12-14/r3.anchor: وقيل: المستقر المكان الذي يستقر فيه المؤمن والكافر وذلك إلى الله لا إلى العبادة

TABRISI:75:12-14/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:12-14/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
TABRISI:75:12-14/r4.claim: Another interpretation makes the settlement the destination and return; it may be temporary or everlasting.
TABRISI:75:12-14/r4.anchor: وقيل: المستقر المصير والمرجع عن ابن مسعود والمستقر على وجهين مستقر إلى أمد ومستقر إلى الأبد

THALABI:v10p84/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p84/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p84/r12.claim: The final settlement of creatures, deeds, and all things is with God; al-Muqatil calls it the terminus, Yaman the return, and the text links this to other verses about returning to God.
THALABI:v10p84/r12.anchor: أي مستقر الخلق وأعمالهم وكل شيء، وقال مقاتل: المنتهى

ELMALILI:75:1-30#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#3/r10.claim: On that Day, settlement and final recourse are to the Lord alone.

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r1.claim: “Mustaqarr” can be a verbal noun for settling or a place noun for the final abode.

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r2.claim: Every servant’s only refuge is God; those fleeing Him find no other shelter, and all finally reach Him or His command.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r2.anchor: O’ndan kaçmak isteyenler de o gün O’ndan başka sığınacak hiçbir penâh bulamazlar.

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r3.claim: Alternatively, God determines whether each person’s final destination is Paradise or Hell.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r3.anchor: insanların varacakları karargâhı cennet mi cehennem mi tâyin etmek Rabbine aittir.

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r4.claim: The address is first to the Prophet, the foremost addressee, and thereby to all people, rather than to the fugitive in the scene.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r4.anchor: seyyid-i muhâtabîn olan Resûl-i Ekrem’e, dolayısıyla da ale’l-umûm insanlara beyân-ı hakikattir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:11/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:11/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:11/r1.claim: On the Resurrection, no refuge or destination exists except God's presence; everyone will gather before Him and be told all good and evil they did or failed to do.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:11/r1.anchor: O gün herkes Allah’ın huzurunda toplanacak ve dünyada yapıp ettikleri ve yapması gerektiği halde yapmadıkları iyi ve kötü ne varsa hepsi ona haber verilecektir

RAZI-FULL:v30p195#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p195#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p195#2/r1.claim: One reading takes al-mustaqarr as “settling”: people cannot settle or turn toward anyone other than their Lord.
RAZI-FULL:v30p195#2/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أن يكون المستقر بمعنى الاستقرار ، بمعنى أنهم لا يقدرون أن يستقروا إلى غيره ، وينصبوا إلى غيره

RAZI-FULL:v30p195#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p195#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p195#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, al-mustaqarr means their destination or place of settlement, Paradise or Hell; God decides by His will whom to admit to either.
RAZI-FULL:v30p195#2/r2.anchor: الثاني : أن يكون المعنى إلى ربك مستقرهم ، أي موضع قرارهم من جنة أو نار ، أي مفوض ذلك إلى مشيئته من شاء أدخله الجنة

STUDYQURAN:75:12/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:12/r1.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:75:12/r1.claim: God alone chooses the final destination where each soul will reside on Judgment Day.
STUDYQURAN:75:12/r1.anchor: God alone who chooses the final destination in which each soul will reside

STUDYQURAN:75:12/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:12/r2.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:75:12/r2.claim: Alternatively, God Himself is each person’s final end.
STUDYQURAN:75:12/r2.anchor: or that God is one’s final end

TAB-FULL:v23p488/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p488/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p488/r1.claim: Every creature’s final settlement is with its Lord, who assigns each creation its place of rest.
TAB-FULL:v23p488/r1.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {إلى ربك يومئذ المستقر} [القيامة: 12] قال: استقر أهل الجنة في الجنة

TAB-FULL:v23p488/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p488/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p488/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says the people of Paradise settle in Paradise and the people of Hell in Hell, citing the Hereafter as the true life.
TAB-FULL:v23p488/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {إلى ربك يومئذ المستقر} [القيامة: 12] قال: استقر أهل الجنة في الجنة، وأهل النار في النار

TAB-FULL:v23p488/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p488/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p488/r3.claim: Qatāda interprets the phrase as the ultimate destination.
TAB-FULL:v23p488/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، {إلى ربك يومئذ المستقر} [القيامة: 12] أي المنتهى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p490#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p490#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p490#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses al-mustaqarr as the destination: everyone returns to God and every affair ends with Him, as other verses say.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p490#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p490#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p490#2/r2.claim: Muqatil says that on that day there is no place to depart from it.

DAMGHANI:v1p374/r17.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p374/r17.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p374/r17.claim: Mustaqarr can mean an endpoint or final destination; examples use it for the sun, a report, and every affair.
DAMGHANI:v1p374/r17.anchor: الثالث المستقر المنتهى قوله تعالى في سورة يس والشمس تجري لمستقر لها

DAMGHANI:v1p387/r15.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p387/r15.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p387/r15.claim: The entry also lists the sense “a little among a great many.”
DAMGHANI:v1p387/r15.anchor: ق ل ل على سبعة أوجه قليل يسير رياء وسمعة لا شيء قليل في كثير

DAMGHANI:v1p387/r16.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p387/r16.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p387/r16.claim: The entry lists the number of the people of Badr as one of its further topics but does not elaborate in this excerpt.
DAMGHANI:v1p387/r16.anchor: لا شيء قليل في كثير عدة أهل بدر عدة قوم طالوت عبد الله بن عباس

DAMGHANI:v1p387/r17.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p387/r17.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p387/r17.claim: The entry lists the number of Saul’s people as one of its further topics but does not elaborate here.
DAMGHANI:v1p387/r17.anchor: قليل في كثير عدة أهل بدر عدة قوم طالوت عبد الله بن عباس

SAMIN-DURR:75:12/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:12/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:75:12/r1.claim: المستقر is the subject and the preceding prepositional phrase its predicate; it can mean settling or the place of settling.
SAMIN-DURR:75:12/r1.anchor: قوله: { المستقر }: مبتدأ، خبره الجار قبله. ويجوز أن يكون مصدرا بمعنى الاستقرار

SAMIN-DURR:75:12/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:12/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:75:12/r2.claim: يومئذ depends on an omitted verb, not مستقر: a verbal noun cannot govern a preceding element, and a place noun has no governing force.
SAMIN-DURR:75:12/r2.anchor: إن كان مكانا فلا عمل له البتة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p209/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p209/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p209/r1.claim: There is no refuge or place of settlement except with God; the one fleeing can turn only to Him.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p209/r1.anchor: والفارُّ يطلب ملجأ يأوي إليه ويعتصم به ويطلب الاستقرار ولكن لا استقرار إلا إلى الله، فإليه وحده المستقر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p209/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p209/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p209/r2.claim: Fronting ‘to your Lord’ restricts the destination and serves the verse ending; fronting ‘that day’ likewise confines this settlement to that day, unlike worldly refuge.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p209/r2.anchor: من جهة المعنى وهو الاختصاص والقصر، وتقتضيه فاصلة الآية أيضاً.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p209/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p209/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p209/r3.claim: ‘To your Lord’ comes first because it answers what the fleeing person is seeking and is the most important part of the answer.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p209/r3.anchor: فقدم له ما يبحث عنه، وقال له: {إلى رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ المستقر} لأنه هو الأهم، وهو المقصود

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p209/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p209/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p209/r4.claim: Rabb means owner, master, governor, nurturer, guardian, and benefactor; it fits because the fugitive returns to his master and the one who manages his affairs.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p209/r4.anchor: فالرب هو المالك والسيّد والمدبّر والمربّي والقيّم والمنعم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p209/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p209/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p209/r5.claim: Mustaqarr is chosen because it can denote settlement as an action, a place, or a time, rather than conveying only one of these senses.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p209/r5.anchor: ذلك أن هذه الكلمة تدل على المصدر بمعنى الاستقرار، وتدل على اسم المكان بمعنى مكان الاستقرار، وتدل على اسم الزمان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p210/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p210/r1.speaker: الكشاف
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p210/r1.claim: Al-Kashshāf reads this as the servants' settlement exclusively with God, the return of their affairs to His judgment (cf. 40:16), or their final place in Paradise or Hell.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p210/r1.anchor: جاء في (الكشاف) في قوله تعالى: {إلى رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ المستقر} : "إلى ربك خاصة (يومئذ) مستقرُّ العباد، أي: استقرارهم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p210/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p210/r2.speaker: البحر المحيط
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p210/r2.claim: Al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ says mustaqarr can mean settlement or its place, Paradise or Hell, whose assignment is according to God's will.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p210/r2.anchor: وجاء في (البحر المحيط) : "المستقر، أي: الاستقرار أو موضع استقرار من جنة أو نار إلى مشيئته تعالى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p210/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p210/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p210/r3.claim: The author adds the time of judgment and dispatch to the other two senses: God decides how long people remain and when they go to their final homes; the word's three senses and cadence make it irreplaceable.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p210/r3.anchor: وتفيد زمان الاستقرار أيضاً، أي أن وقت الفصل بين الخلائق، وسَوقهم إلى مستقرهم عائد إلى مشيئته تعالى

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p71/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p71/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p71/r1.claim: The answer to “Whither to flee?” is that every path closes except refuge with God; towards Him is the destination that Day.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p71/r1.anchor: Except for seeking refuge with God

ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r1.claim: One reading makes God alone the servants’ refuge; another makes Him the sole judge of their affair; a third locates their final abode, Paradise or Hell, in His will.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r1.anchor: أي إليه جل وعلا وحده استقرار العباد أي لا ملجأ ولا منجي لهم غيره عز وجل أو إلى حكمه تعالى استقرار أمرهم لا يحكم فيه غير سبحانه أو إلى مشيئته تعالى موضع قرارهم من جنة أو نار

ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r2.claim: Putting the predicate first marks the exclusivity of the destination or judgment, according to the intended sense of مستقر.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r2.anchor: فتقديم الخبر لأفادة الأختصاص واختلف وجهه حسب اختلاف المراد بمستقر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r3.claim: Kalla la wazar may be God’s words to the person asking where to flee, or the person’s own self-correction after asking.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r3.anchor: وكلا لا وزر يحتمل أن يكون من كلامه تعالى يقال للقائل أين المفر يوم يقوله أو هو مقول اليوم على معنى ليرتدع عن طلب الفرار وتمنيه ذلك اليوم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r4.claim: Al-Alusi takes this as a new explanatory or confirming statement addressed to the Prophet, not part of the person’s speech; he objects to al-Bahr’s contrary reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r4.anchor: والخطاب فيه لسيد المخاطبين صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم ولا يحسن أن يكون

ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r5.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r5.claim: Al-Bahr holds that both “No refuge” and “to your Lord is the destination” continue the human speaker’s words; al-Alusi finds this problematic.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r5.anchor: وفي البحر الظاهر أن قوله تعالى كلا لا وزر إلى ربك يومئذ المستقر من تمام قول الأنسان وقيل هو من كلام الله تعالى لا حكاية عن الأنسان

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:9-12/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:9-12/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:9-12/r9.claim: The servants' final settling is with God alone, or the outcome of their affair is subject to His judgment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:9-12/r9.anchor: إليه وحده استقرار العباد، أو إلى حكمه استقرار أمرهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:9-12/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:9-12/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:9-12/r10.claim: Alternatively, their place of rest depends on God's will: He admits whomever He wills to Paradise or Fire.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:9-12/r10.anchor: أو إلى مشيئته موضع قرارهم يدخل من يشاء الجنة ومن يشاء النار

BIQAI-FULL:v8p245/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p245/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p245/r9.claim: All creation—speaking and silent, its place and time of rest—ultimately lies under God’s judgment and will, outwardly and inwardly; none other rules it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p245/r9.anchor: استقرار الخلق كلهم ناطقهم وصامتهم ومكان قرارهم وزمانه

DURR-FULL:v8p345/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r12.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r12.claim: Qatadah explains the final destination as the point of arrival.
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r12.anchor: عن قتادة قال {لا وزر} قال: لا جبل ولا حرز ولا ملجأ ولا منجى {إلى ربك يومئذ المستقر} قال: المنتهى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p420#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p420#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p420#2/r1.claim: Al-mustaqarr is the final destination and return.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p420#2/r1.anchor: إلى ربك يومئذ المستقر أي المنتهى والمرجع

NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#3/r1.claim: The final destination is exclusively in the hands of the Lord: He wills whom to put in Paradise and whom in Hell.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#3/r1.anchor: مستقر العباد أو موضع قرارهم من جنة أو نار مفوض ذلك لمشيئته

NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#3/r2.claim: “المستقر” can mean the servants' settled state or the place they will settle, Paradise or Hell.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#3/r2.anchor: مستقر العباد أو موضع قرارهم من جنة أو نار
